tone_statements.quote: In the Southern Cushitic languages, the majority of the nouns are toneless and only receive tone through suffixation of high-toned morphemes - see Mous (1993: 21) for Iraqw, Harvey (2018: 76-79) for Gorwaa, Mous (2016: 21) for Alagwa, and Kießling (1994: 25-28) for Burunge. ... In many Cushitic languages, the addition of a high-toned interrogative suffix removes all preceding high tones ... This is also the case for Iraqw and Alagwa (Mous 1993, 2016), and it could well be a phonologized intonational pattern.
tone_statements.locator: §3 'Properties of Cushitic grammar-only tone languages', opening paragraph (nouns toneless, H only via H-toned suffixes, citing Mous 2016: 21 for Alagwa) and §3.3 'Tone behaviour, tone rules' (H-toned interrogative suffix deletes preceding Hs in Iraqw and Alagwa); the 'Kießling (2002, 2004)' pointer is in the §4 'Emerging lexical distinctions' intro; journal pagination 91-106 (SciELO HTML unpaginated)
tone_statements.summary: Restricted/grammatical tone: nouns mostly toneless, H only from H-toned suffixes; H-toned interrogative suffix deletes preceding Hs.

No mention of stress anywhere in the review.
